generic: Live Freeze Dried Lactic Acid Bacteria and Bifidobacteria
cls: Multi-strain probiotic (lactobacilli/lactic-acid bacteria + bifidobacteria) - dietary supplement
pharm: A freeze-dried (lyophilized) combination of live lactic-acid bacteria (e.g., Lactobacillus species) and Bifidobacterium species. As a probiotic it transiently replenishes beneficial gut flora to support digestive balance, especially after antibiotics or during diarrhea. It is marketed as a dietary supplement, not an FDA-approved drug.
quick: Typically ~1-10 billion CFU/day per product label (1 sachet/capsule once-twice daily)
May be taken with or without food; with/after food may improve survival
Generally considered low risk; data limited - follow clinician advice
Generally considered low risk; data limited
No specific adjustment; caution in severe immunocompromise
Symptom response; rare bacteremia/fungemia risk in immunocompromised/central-line patients
summary: This product is a freeze-dried (lyophilized) live mixture of lactic-acid bacteria (lactobacilli) and bifidobacteria taken as a probiotic. It is used to restore and maintain healthy intestinal flora - for example during or after antibiotic therapy, and as supportive treatment for acute and antibiotic-associated diarrhea and some functional digestive complaints. Freeze-drying keeps the organisms dormant and viable until rehydrated in the gut. Such products are regulated as dietary supplements rather than FDA-approved medicines, so the strains, potency (CFU), and quality vary by product and should be taken per the product label. They are generally well tolerated; the main safety concern is rare invasive infection in severely immunocompromised patients or those with central venous catheters.
indications: Probiotic supplementation to restore/maintain healthy intestinal microbial balance, including after antibiotic therapy
Supportive management of acute infectious and antibiotic-associated diarrhea
Symptom support in some functional bowel disorders (supplement use, not an approved drug indication)

dosage.d: Approximately 1-10 billion CFU per day (commonly one sachet/capsule once or twice daily)
dosage.n: Potency and strains vary by product; follow the product label

dosage.d: Per product label during and shortly after the antibiotic course
dosage.n: Separate from antibiotic doses by about 2 hours
Use formulations dosed for children; reconstitute sachets as directed

admin: If a sachet/powder, dissolve in a small amount of water or non-hot food/drink and take promptly; do not use hot liquids (kills the organisms)
May be taken with or without food; taking with or just after food can improve organism survival
If used with an antibiotic, separate dosing by about 2 hours
Refrigerate if directed; freeze-dried products are dormant but lose potency with heat and moisture
Continue for the period advised on the product or by a clinician
moa: As probiotics, the live lactobacilli and bifidobacteria transiently populate the intestine, where they ferment carbohydrates to produce lactic acid and short-chain fatty acids that lower luminal pH and inhibit pathogenic organisms. They compete with pathogens for nutrients and mucosal adhesion sites, produce antimicrobial substances (e.g., bacteriocins), reinforce the intestinal epithelial barrier, and modulate local immune responses. Bifidobacteria are major colonic commensals and lactobacilli predominate in the small intestine, so the combination supports flora across the gut. The organisms do not permanently colonize and are cleared in the stool after the supplement is stopped.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to the product or its components (note: some products contain milk-derived ingredients)
relative: Severe immunocompromise (neutropenia, advanced HIV, transplant, chemotherapy)
Critically ill patients or those with central venous catheters (rare risk of probiotic bacteremia/fungemia)
Acute severe pancreatitis (caution with probiotics in severely ill patients)
Short-gut or major intestinal mucosal disruption
monitor: Resolution or worsening of diarrhea/GI symptoms
Signs of infection in immunocompromised or central-line patients

preg: Probiotics are generally considered low risk in pregnancy because they act locally in the gut, but specific safety data for this combination are limited. Use during pregnancy under the advice of a healthcare professional.
lact: Probiotics are generally considered compatible with breastfeeding and are not expected to reach the infant systemically, but formal data are limited. Use during breastfeeding under the advice of a healthcare professional.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed in renal impairment. Use caution in severely immunocompromised patients regardless of renal status because of the rare risk of invasive infection.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed in hepatic impairment. Standard caution regarding invasive infection applies to severely ill/immunocompromised patients.

moderate: Systemic antibiotics - reduce viability of the live organisms; separate dosing by about 2 hours
Antifungal agents - may affect viability if any yeast-containing combination is co-administered
Immunosuppressants - theoretical increased risk of probiotic-related infection in heavily immunosuppressed patients
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid mixing with hot food or drinks, which kills the organisms.

serious: Probiotic bacteremia/sepsis (rare, essentially limited to severely immunocompromised or central-line patients)
rare: Allergic reaction to product components (including milk-derived ingredients)
emergency: Signs of systemic infection (high fever, rigors) in an immunocompromised or critically ill patient

monitoring: Improvement or persistence of diarrhea/GI symptoms
Signs of infection in high-risk (immunocompromised, central-line, critically ill) patients
counsel: This is a probiotic supplement that helps restore the good bacteria in your gut, often used during or after antibiotics or for diarrhea
Mix sachets in cool (not hot) water or food and take soon after mixing
If you take an antibiotic, take this about 2 hours apart from it
Mild gas or bloating may occur at first and usually settles
Tell your doctor before using probiotics if you have a weakened immune system or a central IV line
See a doctor if diarrhea is severe, bloody, lasts more than a couple of days, or you become dehydrated
pk: Acts locally in the gut; symptom benefit over days
Not applicable - transient intestinal presence, then cleared in stool
Transient colonization; lost within days of stopping
Store per product label; many require refrigeration to maintain potency
pearls: Combination of lactobacilli (small-bowel predominant) and bifidobacteria (colon predominant) gives broad coverage along the gut
Freeze-dried (lyophilized) - dormant and viable until rehydrated; avoid hot liquids and heat/moisture which kill the organisms
Regulated as a dietary supplement, NOT an FDA-approved drug; strains and CFU vary by product
Separate from systemic antibiotics by about 2 hours to preserve viability
Main safety concern is rare probiotic bacteremia in severely immunocompromised or central-line patients - avoid in these groups unless advised
Some products contain milk-derived ingredients - relevant for milk-protein allergy
missed: If you miss a dose, take it when you remember, or skip it and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose. Missing a dose of a probiotic is not harmful.
overdose: Overdose is very unlikely to cause harm; excessive intake may cause transient gas, bloating, or loose stools. Treatment is supportive (reduce the dose or stop temporarily and maintain hydration).
